name: Beret

card.summary: A soft, round wool cap that adds a deliberate, artistic style signal and frames the face, worn to dress up simple outfits or cover hair.

quick.overview:
The beret is a soft, flat-crowned, brimless cap, traditionally of felted wool. It sits close to the head and can be pulled to one side or the back, which changes how it frames the forehead and face.

It began as Basque and Pyrenean shepherd headwear, became a military and then artistic and fashion item, and is used today as a style accessory. No studies have tested its effect on perceived attractiveness.
quick.how: People wear it as a finishing accessory over simple clothing, adjusting the angle and how much forehead shows. Traditional wool berets are described as warm, windproof and waterproof, so they also serve as practical cold-weather hats.
quick.risks: There are no medical risks beyond ordinary hat wear. A snug cap can flatten hair, and styling success depends on fit and face shape.

lead: A beret is a soft, flat-crowned cap, usually made of felted or knitted wool. Similar headwear dates back to the Bronze Age, but the modern form comes from the Basque region and the Pyrenees, where shepherds wore it; commercial production started in the 17th century near Oloron-Sainte-Marie and industrialised in the 19th century.[1]

As a style item it is associated with artistry and intellect and was adopted as sportswear in the 1920s, by jazz musicians, and in the 1960s by activist groups.[1] People use it to add a distinct silhouette, frame the face and hide a hairline or bad hair day.
Military adoption began with the French Chasseurs Alpins in 1889, and it became famous in World War II through Field Marshal Montgomery.[1] No clinical study has examined berets for appearance.

chain: Soft round cap worn at an angle
Changes the frame around forehead and hairline
angle.text: A beret adds a recognisable shape on top of the head and can be angled to show more or less forehead. People wear it as an accessory to give plain outfits a deliberate, artistic feel.

paras: Berets are soft and snug, can be shaped in many ways, and military versions usually include a headband. Traditional wool ones are warm, windproof and waterproof.[1]

Beret-like caps appear from the Bronze Age in northern Europe and in ancient Crete, Italy and Rome. The Basque-style beret was industrialised in the 19th century across southern France, northern Spain and Italy.[1]

The British Royal Tank Regiment's black beret was approved in 1924, and the maroon airborne beret followed in July 1942.[1] In the 1960s the Black Panther Party (1966) and Brown Berets (1967) wore berets as symbols.[1]

Berets have long suggested artistry and intellect, linked in the encyclopedia article to Rembrandt and Richard Wagner. In Spain the beret's association with rural stereotypes reduced its popularity in the 20th century.[1]
